subject: Program sweetener — revenue-share vs. one-time credit
messages:
From: Sam Yates <sam@launchbridge.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: finance@launchbridge.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + question on cohort sweetener structure

Hey Connor — great demo last week, thanks. LaunchBridge is finalizing the curriculum cohort for August and we want Redwood to be the recommended inference partner. Before we get to contract terms, two quick practical asks:

1) We usually give each startup a $2k–$5k vendor credit to cover dev onboarding. Can Redwood provide a one-time onboarding credit for cohort startups, or do you prefer a different mechanism?
2) Alternatively, we explored a revenue-share pilot (2% of any LaunchBridge-referred paid deals in Q4) that would help offset program fees. Open to either; curious what is easier for Redwood ops + finance.

Attached is a short scope doc for the MVP integration (LB_MVP_scope_v1.pdf). We need a quick decision — internal budget sign-off Thursday.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Yates | Partnerships Lead, LaunchBridge
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Yates <sam@launchbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + question on cohort sweetener structure

Hi Sam — really excited about this (team loved the demo). Short answers up front: we can do a one-time onboarding credit for cohort startups, and we can also pilot a revenue-share structure — but they have different operational trade-offs.

High-level: onboarding credit
- Pros: simple to administer, predictable cost, shows immediate goodwill to founders.
- Cons: hard to gate to only founders who convert; may be consumed by heavy experimentation.

Revenue-share pilot
- Pros: aligns incentives over time, lower upfront cost for us if conversion is low.
- Cons: requires tracking/referral attribution and a small finance integration; we typically avoid revenue-sharing outside strategic channel partners.

Given pace, quickest path is a limited one-time credit tied to onboarding completion (i.e., redeemable after a smoke-test integration). If you want rev-share, we can surface a term sheet but would need: referral attribution rules, a 12-month lookback, and finance/GA sign-off.

I've looped in Ben and Marissa to confirm pricing boundaries. Can you confirm estimated headcount (number of startups) in the cohort and whether credits should be transferable?

Best —
Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: pricing cap + governance on cohort credits

Connor/Marissa — quick internal note before we respond to Sam with numbers. A few guardrails:

- Max aggregate exposure: we should cap cohort credits for LaunchBridge at $25k total (to keep pilot leakage limited).
- Per-startup credit: $2,500 recommended (matches program ask and gives founders meaningful runway).
- Eligibility: require a minimal verification step (dev verification checklist + ashburn smoke test) before credit release.
- Transferability: do not allow transfer between startups. That complicates bookkeeping.
- Rev-share: not preferred unless LB covers tracking costs or we link to HubSpot referral IDs for auto-attach. If LB wants rev-share, request they accept a minimum guarantee ($5k) to make the pilot meaningful.

If Marissa/Laura OK, I'll propose these terms back to Sam and attach a simple T&Cs doc (RI_credit_term_draft.docx).

Ben
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sam Yates <sam@launchbridge.com>, Tasha Patel <tasha.patel@venturehub.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + question on cohort sweetener structure

Sam — thanks for the scope doc and context. We like LaunchBridge and are happy to pilot cohort credits with the following proposal:

Summary proposal (Redwood -> LaunchBridge cohort)
- Program credit: $2,500 per startup, capped at 10 startups (total exposure $25,000).
- Release trigger: credit becomes redeemable after a passed integration checklist and a first successful inference call to production (smoke test).
- Transferability: credits non-transferable and expire after 90 days if unused.
- Rev-share option: we can pilot a 1.5% revenue-share on qualified LaunchBridge referrals for 12 months, but only if LaunchBridge provides automated attribution (HubSpot referral ID) and guarantees a minimum payout of $5,000. We prefer the credit path for simplicity.
- Billing: credits will appear as an invoice credit memo against the startup's first invoice; no upfront cash movement.

Tasha — copying for a quick legal sanity check on the credit T&Cs. We can push a short one-pager. Sam, if that aligns, we'll send a one-page credit T&C and a statement of work for the integration.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, GTM Partnerships, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: RI_credit_term_draft.docx (stub) — simple T&Cs: eligibility, expiration, non-transferability, attribution requirements.
From: Sam Yates <sam@launchbridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: finance@launchbridge.com, tasha.patel@venturehub.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + question on cohort sweetener structure

Marissa — this looks great and aligns with the cohort finance model. A couple of quick clarifications before I route to our CFO:

- Can the credit expiry be 120 days instead of 90? A few founders may take longer to flip their pilots.
- For the smoke test: can Redwood accept a self-attestation + CI test report if we provide logs, rather than requiring a managed Ashburn test?
- On rev-share: we will take the 1.5% proposal and provide the HubSpot referral ID flow if we trial it — but we will not be able to guarantee the $5k minimum for this first pilot.

If you can confirm the 120-day expiry and flexible smoke-test acceptance, I can get sign-off today and we can exchange the T&C one-pager + SOW.

Thanks — Sam
// End of thread
